title: Design brief
description: Product-tier (P) narrative document (doc 11 §2, §6). Captures the design intent, audience and tone, and constraints for a project, and links to the separate F6 design-system artifact (DTCG ThemeDoc, doc 11 §2). Canonical form: narrative markdown — the envelope plus a `data:` block and required markdown sections. Authored by the intake agent from the creation conversation; therefore `meta.source` (conversation grounding) is required.

type.description: Selects this schema. Must be the literal string `design-brief`.

source.description: Conversation grounding (doc 11 §4). Product-tier documents are derived from the creation conversation, so at least one source span (run + message range) is required to trace this brief back to the user's words.

data.description: Structured content of the design brief: the link to the design-system artifact and optional token hints.

design_system_reference.description: Reference to the F6 design-system artifact this brief informs (the DTCG ThemeDoc, doc 11 §2). An `artifact://` reference when a design system exists, or null when none has been produced yet. The design system is a separate-but-linked artifact (doc 11 §2, ruled); the corresponding typed edge is recorded under `meta.links.informs`.

anyOf.description: An `artifact://` reference to the F6 ThemeDoc artifact.
No design-system artifact exists yet for this project.

token_hints.description: Optional, ordered design-token hints guiding the design system (e.g. palette, type-scale, spacing intentions). Each entry is either a plain markdown string or an object carrying a `hint` markdown field; agents may mix the two forms.

anyOf.description: A single token hint expressed as markdown prose.
A single token hint as an object, allowing future structured fields alongside the prose.

hint.description: The token hint as markdown prose (e.g. 'Primary palette leans cool, high-contrast for accessibility').

sections.description: Required narrative sections, keyed by stable section id; each value is a markdown string (doc 11 §5).

intent.description: What the product should feel like and why: the design goal, the emotional and experiential intent, and the outcome a successful design achieves. State the intent, not implementation details.

audience-and-tone.description: Who the design speaks to and how. Describe the target audience (tie to product-charter personas where relevant) and the voice and tone the experience should convey (e.g. authoritative, playful, minimal).

constraints.description: Bounds the design must respect: brand requirements, accessibility standards, platform or device targets, performance limits, and any explicit non-goals. State each constraint as a checkable expectation.
